case_name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Criminal Appeal No. 1277 of 2014
Arnesh Kumar ... Appellant
versus
State of Bihar and Another ... Respondents
Coram: Chandramauli Kr. Prasad and Pinaki Chandra Ghose, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 02 July, 2014

CHANDRAMAULI KR. PRASAD, J.:
1. The petitioner apprehending arrest in a case registered under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 had approached this Court for grant of anticipatory bail after his prayer was rejected by the High Court of Patna.

5. Arrest brings humiliation, curtails freedom and casts scars forever. No arrest can be made in a mechanical manner merely because the allegation pertains to a cognizable offence. Section 41 of the Code of Criminal Procedure clearly stipulates the conditions precedent before an arrest can be effected without warrant for offences carrying imprisonment up to seven years.

6. The police officer must satisfy himself about the necessity of arrest based on parameters specified in Section 41(1)(b) CrPC: to prevent the person from committing any further offence, for proper investigation, or to prevent tampering with evidence.

11. We direct that in all cases where offences are punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years or which may extend to seven years, whether with or without fine:
(1) Police officers shall not arrest the accused unnecessarily without satisfying the checklist under Section 41(1)(b) CrPC.
(2) Notice of appearance in terms of Section 41A CrPC shall be served on the accused within two weeks from the date of institution of the case.
(3) Failure to comply with these directions shall render police officers liable for departmental action and contempt of court.
